title: PROBABILISTIC DATA STRUCTURES
subtitle: Trade a small, known error for a tiny fraction of the memory.
footer: System Design, Step by Step · core concepts

blocks.text: Is X in the set? "Definitely not" or "probably yes". ~10 bits per item ≈ 1% false positives.
How often? +1 in each row, read the minimum. Never undercounts; heavy hitters are accurate.
How many distinct? Leading-zero runs across 16k registers: ±0.8% in 12 KB, mergeable.

items: Bloom: no deletes, size for the expected count
HLL: approximate only; never for billing
Say the error and why it is acceptable

blocks.text: "Seen URLs live in a Bloom filter: 10 billion at 1% is about 12 GB, and a false positive just skips a page. Unique viewers per video use HyperLogLog: 12 KB each, under 1% error, and hourly sketches merge into daily."
